The Hebrew file transliterated it as a fund name, so it was not an acronym. Removed; Pitango, Grove Ventures and OurCrowd were each confirmed live. Grove Ventures is its full name.

FABRICATED DIRECTIVE removed (CRITICAL): the skill taught  in Marp front matter, in three files. Marpit global directives are exactly headingDivider, lang, style and theme, confirmed against the directives doc. There is no dir directive, unrecognised keys are silently ignored, so a deck relying on it renders LTR with no error.

WRONG fixed (CRITICAL): the skill said Marp bundles a Chromium instance and told users to check marp --version to confirm it. The marp-cli README says you have to install Chrome, Edge or Firefox to convert to PDF, PPTX or images; the standalone binaries bundle Node.js, not a browser. The debugging step was impossible and the dependency claim was inverted.

BROKEN CODE fixed (MAJOR): enable_font_embedding() in references/pptx-rtl-patches.md started with prs.presentation, which raises AttributeError on python-pptx 1.0.2 (verified by execution). It then wrote embedTrueTypeFonts onto a p:presentationPr element it created as a child of p:presentation, but presentationPr is the root of a separate part and the flag belongs on p:presentation itself. Replaced with a one-liner on prs._element that was executed and confirmed to round-trip into ppt/presentation.xml.

WRONG fixed (MAJOR): the intra-token bidi section explained reordering as caused by run boundaries and told the author to keep a token in one run. Verified against UAX #9: the algorithm runs over the paragraph character stream and a DrawingML run boundary is not an input, so splitting or merging runs changes nothing. The real cause is a neutral character between two strong runs. Fix 2 was a no-op and is now stated as such.

WRONG fixed (MAJOR): fix 3 told users to make an LTR island with LRM and RLM, and its own literal example started with RLM+LRM rather than the LRM its prose specified. Marks are strong characters, not isolation; only LRI/PDI creates an island. Fix 3 now uses LRI/PDI and says why marks do not work here.

FIXED (MAJOR): neither shipped theme CSS carried the /* @theme name */ metadata comment Marpit requires, so a deck saying theme: rtl-hebrew could not resolve it by name and would silently fall back to the default LTR theme. Added to both.

IMPROVED: the Google Slides section hedged (check the API reference before relying on a specific field name), which reads like a hallucination even though the underlying statement was fine. The field is documented: ParagraphStyle.direction with LEFT_TO_RIGHT / RIGHT_TO_LEFT via UpdateParagraphStyleRequest, and direction is NOT inherited, defaulting to LEFT_TO_RIGHT. Named it, and added the non-inheritance caveat, which is a real Hebrew gotcha the skill had omitted.

FIXED (MINOR): scripts/create-presentation.py passed a magic 1 to add_shape commented as MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE. That enum has no RECTANGLE member; the correct symbol is MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE. Now imported and used by name.

MY OWN REGRESSION, caught by both panel agents: my Chromium fix used a string replacement that ended mid-sentence, leaving the closing words "Chromium is bundled." dangling at the end of the corrected paragraph in BOTH language files. The paragraph then said Marp does not bundle a browser and, two sentences later, that Chromium is bundled. A partial string replace on prose is how a correction re-breaks itself.

CRITICAL fixed (both agents, verified by execution and by rendering): the skill claimed column index 0 is the rightmost column in an RTL table, and told users to pre-reverse their data on that basis. Neither the script nor any reference helper ever set the rtl attribute on <a:tblPr>, which is what actually reverses column order; they only patched each cell <a:pPr>, which is text direction INSIDE a cell. The shipped deck had <a:tblPr firstRow=1 bandRow=1> with no rtl, so every generated table came out mirrored, AND the pre-reversal advice reversed it a second time. Fixed in scripts/create-presentation.py (new set_table_rtl), in add_rtl_table and set_table_rtl in the reference, and in Gotcha 5 in both languages. Verified: the deck now emits <a:tblPr firstRow=1 bandRow=1 rtl=1>.

NOTE ON VERIFICATION LIMITS: PowerPoint honours tblPr@rtl; LibreOffice Impress ignores it, which one agent confirmed by rendering with and without the attribute and getting identical output. So the fix could not be visually confirmed in this environment. The skill now says so explicitly rather than asserting the render.

FIXED: the reference usage example was column-reversed relative to the script under the same stated rule, and its comment named a header (צמיחה) that was not in its own table. Both now use natural reading order and agree with the script.

FIXED: references/marp-rtl-guide.md Known Limitations asserted that Marp renders table columns left-to-right even in RTL mode. CSS specifies that direction on a table determines column ordering, and one agent measured it in headless Chrome (source index 0 at x=401 of a 600px box, i.e. rightmost). The advice that followed happened to be right; the stated mechanism was backwards.

CRITICAL fixed: the skill's central technique (set_paragraph_rtl) injected a child <a:rtl val="1"/> element into <a:pPr>, which is NOT schema-valid per OOXML (ISO/IEC 29500). Paragraph-level RTL is the boolean `rtl` ATTRIBUTE on <a:pPr> / <a:lvl1pPr>..<a:lvl9pPr> (what PowerPoint itself writes). Fixed to pPr.set('rtl','1') (and drop any stale child) in scripts/create-presentation.py, references/pptx-rtl-patches.md, SKILL.md and SKILL_HE.md. Re-tested: 17 paragraphs carry rtl="1" as an attribute, valid 5-slide deck.

CRITICAL fixed (round 2, Expert + own datypic/ECMA-376 verification): DrawingML has NO <a:rtl> element at ALL (datypic e-a_rtl-1.html is 404) and <a:rPr> (CT_TextCharacterProperties) has no rtl attribute, so there is no run-level direction toggle. The original run-level LTR override (<a:rtl val="0"/> on <a:rPr> in add_english_run/set_run_ltr/add_mixed) was therefore schema-invalid (a WordprocessingML <w:rtl/> concept ported into DrawingML); PowerPoint silently ignored it. Removed all run-level <a:rtl> writes: inline English/digits render LTR via the Unicode bidi algorithm, and ambiguous mixed-script tokens are isolated with LRM/LRI/PDI in the text (which the skill already documented). Re-tested: 0 invalid <a:rtl> elements at paragraph OR run level, deck still renders mixed Hebrew/English correctly. Also fixed the slide-master advice (dropped the invalid <a:defRPr> child <a:rtl> suggestion), repointed the OOXML reference to the datypic DrawingML schema, and switched the table currency anchor from a HAIR SPACE (U+200A, no bidi effect) to LRM (U+200E).
